gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the lightest unit also delivered the most measured energy: Notebookcheck drew just over 1,900 Wh from the 35.7 lb Anker SOLIX S2000 at about 250 W, against the 1,710 Wh GearLab measured from the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2, which GearLab weighed at 38.9 lb.
standout_why: I opened three of the results. powerbencher.com (cited) lists the S2000 at 35.7 lb and the Jackery at 39.5 lb but says 'We did not test these units' and uses an assumed 85% usable figure. offgridbenchmark.com says 'I have not tested this unit' and also assumes 85%. slopsheets.com uses maker capacity and weight only and omits the S2000. None carries a measured Wh, a scale weight or a measured idle draw. Not compared: solargenreview.com and jackery.com returned HTTP 429, and I did not open keptpowered, thiswatt, powerstations.reviews, smartgadgetkit, the Jackery blog or the Lowe's manual PDF.
decides: It confirms the Anker SOLIX S2000 as the pick. On a scale the Jackery comes out 0.6 lb lighter than the 39.5 lb the rival pages list, but that is still 3.2 lb more than Anker's 35.7 lb. The measured energy does not reverse the order either: about 1,900 Wh (Notebookcheck, 250 W) against 1,710 Wh (GearLab), and 6 W idle against about 17 W (The Solar Lab, both units). The two Wh figures come from different labs at different loads, so the page should present them side by side, not as one test. The S2000's catch is unchanged: 1,500 W continuous, and GearJunkie's roughly 1,800 W planer tripped it.

findings.label: Usable AC energy, measured by Notebookcheck
findings.value: just over 1,900 Wh (95% of the 2,000 Wh Notebookcheck lists)
findings.source_title: 2 kilowatt-hours have never been this light: Anker Solix S2000 power station review (Notebookcheck, Marcus Schwarten, 2026-10-07)
findings.note: Continuous AC load of around 250 W. Against Anker's 35.7 lb: 1,900 / 35.7 = about 53 Wh delivered per lb (my arithmetic).

findings.label: Charging loss and round trip, measured by Notebookcheck
findings.value: just over 2,400 Wh from the wall for a full charge; just over 82% reached the battery; round trip about 78%
findings.source_title: 2 kilowatt-hours have never been this light: Anker Solix S2000 power station review (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: Charged at a maximum of 1,100 W. Noise around 35 dB at standard charging speed. UPS bypass consumption around 3 W.

findings.label: Self-drain with AC left on, Notebookcheck
findings.value: just over 10% of the battery per 24 hours
findings.source_title: 2 kilowatt-hours have never been this light: Anker Solix S2000 power station review (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: 10% of 2,010 Wh over 24 h is about 8 W average (my arithmetic). That is higher than The Solar Lab's 6 W and ESS News' roughly 2 W.

findings.label: Weight and 'lightest' statement, Notebookcheck
findings.value: 16.2 kg (35.7 lb); 'the lightest 2-kWh power station we have come across so far'
findings.source_title: 2 kilowatt-hours have never been this light: Anker Solix S2000 power station review (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: The 16.2 kg sits in the review's datasheet table, and the article does not say the unit was put on a scale. Do not write 'Notebookcheck measured 16.2 kg'; the desk note overstates it. Notebookcheck lists the C2000 Gen 2 at 18.9 kg, 2.7 kg heavier.

findings.label: Maker's weight and idle figures (Anker US page)
findings.value: 35.7 lbs (16.2 kg); 2010Wh; 1500W AC; Active Idle Power 6W; System Standby Power 2W
findings.note: Footnotes: the 6 W claim is 'based on Anker internal testing' against selected 2 kWh stations as of 2026-05-19; 88% efficiency at a 100 W load is also Anker's internal test. The fetched content showed no price and no shipping notice.

findings.label: Efficiency and idle draw, measured by The Solar Lab
findings.value: 91% efficiency; about 6 W idle with the inverter on, 2 W with it off; AC charge empty to full in about 1 h 47 min
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S2000 Review: The Ultimate Compact Home Backup Power Station? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The page gives no test load or method for the 91%, and shows no author or date beyond 'Copyright 2026'.

findings.label: Idle drain and charge time, ESS News
findings.value: 100% to 99% after 10 hours with AC on and no load (about 2 W average); about 1.2 h to 80% and 1.7 h to 100% on AC
findings.source_title: Anker Solix S2000 review: 2 kWh power station built for the long haul (ESS News, Andrew Riha, 2026-05-19)
findings.note: The drain is read off the unit's own 1% display steps, so the 2 W is coarse.

findings.label: Fridge runtime and overload, GearJunkie
findings.value: ran a Samsung refrigerator/freezer 34 h 15 min to 0%; a planer rated about 1,800 W tripped the overload
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S2000 review (GearJunkie, Nick Belcaster, 2026-07-30)
findings.note: Fridge set to 37°F / -2°F. A toaster at about 850 W ran fine. Weight is the spec figure; the review does not say it was weighed.

findings.label: Weight on GearLab's scale
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 Review (OutdoorGearLab, Chris McNamara, 2025-11-03)
findings.note: 'Measured weight' row. That is 0.6 lb under the 39.5 lb listed on powerbencher.com and slopsheets.com (both read 2026-11-27), and 3.2 lb over Anker's 35.7 lb for the S2000.

findings.label: Usable AC energy, measured by GearLab
findings.note: Measured through the AC outlets on GearLab's light-bulb load bank. The same review's Power Output section says 1,740 Wh; the spec table and the roundup (updated 2026-07-23) both say 1,710 Wh. Charge 0-100% took 2.5 h, an average of 817 Wh/hr. 1,710 / 38.9 = about 44 Wh delivered per lb (my arithmetic).

findings.label: Efficiency and idle draw, measured by The Solar Lab
findings.value: 90% efficiency; about 17 W idle with the inverter on; about 5 days from full to empty with no load
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 2000 V2 Review: Should You Buy It or the 2000 Plus? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: Same reviewer measured 6 W on the S2000. The 11 W difference is about 264 Wh per 24 h with the inverter left on (my arithmetic). No test load or date on the page.

findings.label: Reviewer's usable-capacity estimate, Techreviewer
findings.value: about 1,700–1,800 Wh usable; about 2.5 h mains charge; weight listed 17.5 kg
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 review (Techreviewer, Christian Matenar, 2026-03-18)
findings.note: An estimate with no stated load, not a logged test. The page does not say the 17.5 kg was weighed. It is consistent with GearLab's figure.

findings.label: Usable AC energy, measured by Notebookcheck
findings.value: about 1,600 Wh at a 200 W load (just under 79% of 2,048 Wh); about 1,850 Wh at 1,800 W (roughly 90%)
findings.source_title: 11.6 kg lighter than its predecessor: Powerstation Anker Solix C2000 Gen 2 review (Notebookcheck, Marcus Schwarten, 2026-02-24, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: Same reviewer as the S2000 test. At a similar light load the S2000 delivered about 300 Wh more (1,900 vs 1,600 Wh) while listed 2.7 kg lighter. Weight 18.9 kg (41.7 lb) is from the datasheet table. Charging took almost 2,350 Wh from the wall, 87% stored. Noise about 35 dB at 1 m under high load.

findings.label: What the cited rival roundup says about testing
findings.value: "We did not test these units"; usable figures assume 85% reaches the outlet
findings.source_title: Best 2000Wh Power Stations (2026) - Runtime and Weight (powerbencher.com)
findings.note: It lists the S2000 at 35.7 lb / 2,010 Wh, the Jackery 2000 v2 at 39.5 lb / 2,042 Wh, the EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max at 50.7 lb and the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 at 53.35 lb, all maker figures. offgridbenchmark.com and slopsheets.com (read the same day) also carry no measurements.

unsourced: A scale weight for the Anker SOLIX S2000: Notebookcheck, TechRadar, GearJunkie, CleanTechnica, ESS News and The Solar Lab all give 16.2 kg / 35.7 lb / 'about 36 lb' as a spec, and none says it weighed the unit.
Jackery's own weight and price for the Explorer 2000 v2: jackery.com returned HTTP 429 to both WebFetch and storecheck.py, so the 39.5 lb here comes from rival pages, not the maker.

Today's Anker US store price and ship time for the S2000: the storecheck.py search returned HTTP 404 and the fetched page content showed no price and no shipping notice, so the 7-13 week delay in the desk notes is not re-confirmed.

Named measurements for the heavier 2 kWh rows (Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO, BLUETTI Elite 200 V2, EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max, DJI Power 2000, Dabbsson 2000L): not researched within the call budget. GearLab's roundup has none of them with test data.
A decibel figure for the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 from a named reviewer: GearLab and Techreviewer describe the fan only in words.

One lab testing the S2000 and the Jackery 2000 v2 at the same load: the Wh figures come from Notebookcheck (250 W) and GearLab (light-bulb load bank, load not stated on the pages read). Only The Solar Lab's idle and efficiency figures cover both units.
